items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: Jack Sheen, he opened up and he said, Rizzley, get me a band... I went on, he choice me and I went with Rizzley. Played drum with Rizzley a while... Jack Sheen's, it's called Jack Sheen's Place.

ctx.x: Yeah, I knew him in New York too. Nice guy.

And we stuck around there, old Frankie Dooson. Stayed there a little while. So here comes Walter Deku. Next block from the woman to play at the bungalow. So I go ahead and work. I jump in for a little more money. Them times, you know, money was money. Dollar was a dollar. Sure. So the Walter Deku line up was. Old Man Dutre on clarinet. Old Man Joe Howard on cornet. Walter Deku on piano and myself on drums. And Big Eye Louie on clarinet. Old Man Dutre is a double. Big Eye Louie couldn't double. Well, that went on…

items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: Jack pie either he's a preacher now... he used to play on the bugle... we had a three piece four piece band the bugle the client and the bass drum and the snare drum

very first job I ever played we had a family called needs to give penny part to play the street I used to be a really called Jack pie either he's a preacher now he lives in the best move Alabama and he used to play on the bugle you know corner to Jack pie you guys everybody know the more Jack pie we had a three piece four piece band the bugle the client and the bass drum and the snare drum round in May the 30th of May we used to go to Chalmette yeah wash all up down the street with them folks you know it's got to…

And this old, this old Nancy, Lorenzo Stahl, he was using Lorenzo Stahl on a band. I remember that good. See, now that was a, that's what all he used to use around here. People call us a Dixon Lane. That been going on. Sure. For years, that been going. We were raised like that. We just didn't use no piano.
